name: fx-first-class-configuration-provenance-and-9c5e
instr:
Fx cannot attach stable provenance labels to configuration or recover the same operation identity across nested modules, diagnostics, and initialization failures. Add `Label` to wrap options, with the nearest label governing each target while preserving its complete root-to-leaf module path.

Every labeled `Provide`, `Supply`, `Invoke`, `Populate`, `Decorate`, and `Replace` target gets its distinct `OperationKind` and stable zero-based position. Preserve annotations, synthesized types, eager and module ordering, scoping, typing, `Private` visibility, graph semantics, errors, events, logging, and fxtest behavior. `Populate` remains a population operation through its generated invocation, including dependency-resolution failures.

Attribute failures to the operation and target that failed, never a containing label or unexecuted target. `AttributedError` and `AttributionOf` must preserve the original error through Go error chaining. An annotated nested invoke keeps its sentinel error while attribution identifies only its failing function and module. A labeled Populate dependency failure reaches fxtest through its established fatal path with recoverable population provenance and the original resolution error. `fxtest.New` must use that fatal path without changing construction or logging.

Corresponding `fxevent` records carry identical provenance across paired success and failure events; provenance-free records remain zero-value compatible. Every event retains the correct target
